subject: Re: Encord & Oléa Médical
text:
Hello Skander,
Thanks for the update.

We’d need to know more about the overall ergonomics of the viewer as far this type of features (slice position and annotation sync) is concerned.
What is shown in the video requires to many manipulations to sync and propagate annotation modifications across series.

Here is a typically scenario we’d like to see an Encord DEMO on:

  1.  Say we have a project where the annotation tasks contain 4 different series by task to address 4 different contrasts of a same acquisition : T1, T2, T2_FLAIR and T1_GADO (which have been initially co-registered and resampled)
  2.  How these “annotation tasks” shall be prepared and imported as Nifti files into a Project / Dataset / Dataunits / Image Sequences (or other) ?
  3.  How can the viewer associated to this project / annotation tasks be automatically setup to display the 4 series side by side on a 2x2 grid layout ?
  4.  How can the volume (slice position) be automatically sync so that when the user moves to another slice in one of the 4 series, it moves the to the same slice in the other 3 series in the same time ?
  5.  How can the annotation be live synced across views ? => the user modifies the label in one of the window, this shall propagate in live to the other 3 windows.

Note:
This example covers a 4-series-by-task annotation project approach with a viewer setup with a 2x2 grid layout.
Now, if a project needs only 2 series (or even 1 series), the viewer shall automatically adapt to dual (side-by-side) or mono window layout.

FYI, these features are natively available in Redbrick UI / import process and are key features for our annotators.

Thanks and regards,
JF

subject: RE: Redlines for Encord MSA
text:
Thank you Nick.

Unfortunately it seems like there’s a measure of “one step back” here. There had been a baseline agreement on Encord’s responsibility for Deliverables which was walked back. This stems from 10.1 and 10.2. To help drive the conversation, it’d be important to understand why Encord fully disclaims its liability for its service and how the deliverables are created. We thought to have drawn an agreed-upon delineation. But it appears not?

That said, there is some progress on 11.4. But there is no “baseline cap” that would apply to non-specified claims. Alastair, happy to discuss tomorrow but setting our sights on supercaps seems to have disclocated the starting point. I’m sure our intent is not, by silence, to create uncapped liability.

That said, as previously mentioned, uncapped liability for indemnification will not be acceptable to Invisible. Especially not given that Encord has walked back its previous position on Deliverables and IP.

On the topic of Usage Data, could you please check internally whether the definition still stands given the deployment scenario? If so, then we wish to understand the “call-home” functions that will be deployed. Though we’ll add that Encord is not to train AI models based on Usage Data, there remains a sensitivity around the scope of this definition. Clarifications will prove helpful to resolve this point.

Many thanks,

Paul
